pilotFindings.kind: the draft FAILED the novel prediction CP1 registered
pilotFindings.found: The first draft of site-model.ts put the promotion refusal ahead of P-219's superseded-envelope refusal. An atom that is both unpromoted and derived from setback law the sheet no longer follows would then have printed 'not depth-warm verified' where it previously printed 'Buildable area withheld: the buildable-envelope atom on file was derived from setback values this study no longer follows ... Pending a re-baked envelope.'
pilotFindings.whyItMatters: Both refuse, so no figure leaked either way -- the defect is that a customer-visible sentence would have changed silently, on a surface no falsifier in this dispatch asked to change. Two rules disagreeing about one atom is the CTRL-1 shape.
pilotFindings.resolution: Prediction was registered first, the draft was measured against it, it failed, and P-219's more specific sentence was put back in front of the gate. The correction is its own commit (32b5669) with the reason in the message, and the probe now asserts both directions: unpromoted+superseded refuses by P-219's sentence, and PROMOTED+superseded ALSO refuses -- the two gates are not each other's fallback.
pilotFindings.honestNote: Whether to file this as a defect or as a design correction is a judgement; it is recorded as a correction to a draft that was never pushed, not as a shipped bug.

pilotFindings.kind: decode instrument, three separate false readings
pilotFindings.found: (a) The FIRST probe failure was an assertion too weak to be evidence: `expect(decoded).not.toContain(String(ATOM_AREA_SQ_FT))` is satisfied by a bare digit run that could be any table figure or coincidental digits in a content stream. It was replaced by the figure's actual spellings -- '6,309 sq ft', the grouped '6,309', the ungrouped '6309 sq ft', and the local derive '2,309 sq ft' -- plus '% of lot'. (b) The refusal sentence is DRAWN ACROSS A WRAPPED LINE, so it arrives as several text-showing operands; a substring assertion against the raw stream fails even though the sentence is on the page. (c) Inter's ligature glyphs come back through the decoder's beginbfchar CMap as Unicode PRESENTATION FORMS -- 'verified', 'file' and 'figure' decode with U+FB01, not 'f'+'i' -- so no plain-ASCII needle matches drawn prose containing one.
pilotFindings.whyItMatters: (a) would have shipped a test that passes for the wrong reason; (b) and (c) would each have been 'fixed' by weakening the assertion to a single word, which would have made the probe unable to measure the thing the dispatch asked it to measure.
pilotFindings.resolution: The probe now has two explicit views with the split documented in the file: the RAW decoded stream for what must NOT be printed (a figure cannot hide from it), and `drawnProse()` -- the decoder's space-joined reconstruction, ligature-folded, whitespace-collapsed -- for what MUST be printed. The section markers carry a control byte before the word, so the helper locates the word itself, following sheet-standard.test.ts's own convention.
pilotFindings.transferable: LESSON for the fleet: a decoded-PDF substring assertion is only evidence if you can say which of the decoder's three reconstructions you meant and why. The refusal-by-wrap problem and the ligature problem will hit every future prose assertion in this repo.

pilotFindings.kind: a citation in the code was wrong until it was read at source
pilotFindings.found: The new predicate's header comment cited hauska-map's mirror as 'packages/retrieval/src/serving-sweep/vendor/atom-chain-to-facets.ts:165-175'. No such file exists. The predicate is at apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/atom-chain-to-facets.ts:116-127.
pilotFindings.whyItMatters: A provenance pointer that does not resolve is worse than none: it tells a future editor the mirror is somewhere it is not, and the whole reason the comment exists is that four predicates read this fact in three repos.
pilotFindings.resolution: Checked at source, wrong path removed, real path and line range cited, plus an explicit note that this lane's fixtures are the same answers the P-249 sibling is told to use so the divergence test between them agrees.

pilotFindings.kind: three checked-in fixtures encoded the superseded rule
pilotFindings.found: author.test.ts, pdf/__tests__/feasibility.test.ts and pdf/__tests__/render.test.ts each built an atom-backed buildable envelope with no marker and expected a printed figure -- i.e. they assert the exact behaviour A-180 outlaws.
pilotFindings.whyItMatters: They are not wrong-looking tests; they were correct under the rule that shipped yesterday. Silently deleting or weakening them would have destroyed coverage of their real subjects (the P-248 seam, P-159's one-figure-per-document control, the rendered callout).
pilotFindings.resolution: Each fixture now supplies the promotion the production path reads, with a comment naming P-261 and pointing at the new probe for the refusal case. Their subjects are untouched. Counting rule: 3 files, 3 fixtures, 3 comment blocks; the refusals they used to imply are now measured in exactly one place.
